title: Priority Escrow & Commit Bands for Enterprise Hosted API Requests (streaming + toolchains)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define and pilot a 'Priority Escrow' mechanism plus tiered 'Commit Bands' to handle high-cost, high-risk enterprise feature requests to the Hosted API (multi-turn streaming + tool/function calling + structured outputs). The goal is to provide predictable capacity and SLA guarantees for vetted enterprise customers while limiting operational and cost exposure for Redwood.
background: We increasingly see enterprise customers requesting immediate high-throughput streaming/toolcall integrations with tight latency and audit requirements. Current intake gates (eligibility questionnaires, SLA scoring) surface risk but do not provide a pragmatic mechanism to reserve capacity or financially account for bursty, multimodal workloads. Teams often scramble to provision Dedicated capacity or make ad-hoc exceptions, creating variability in unit economics and reliability.
proposal: Introduce two linked constructs: (1) Priority Escrow — a short-term, refundable credit hold applied at onboarding that reserves a commit allowance for a defined window (e.g., 30/90 days) and triggers a lightweight readiness review; (2) Commit Bands — discrete tiers of reserved throughput and feature entitlements (e.g., Band A: guaranteed 500 concurrent token streams, Band B: 200 streams + toolcall concurrency) with explicit cost multipliers and rollback rules. Apply a prioritized checklist for qualification (security posture, integration complexity, expected qps, data residency, fallback plan) and an automated mapping from intake signals to recommended Commit Band and escrow amount.
acceptance_criteria: Escrow flow implemented in intake UI with three-step UX: estimate, confirm hold amount, finalize readiness review
Automated mapping rule-set produces a Commit Band recommendation for 90% of enterprise inbound requests in pilot cohort
Playbook documented: eligibility checklist, rollback triggers, SLA handoff to support/ops
Pilot with 3 active enterprise customers; telemetry shows reduced emergency Dedicated provisioning events vs baseline
Billing and refund path validated with finance for escrow holds and commit reconciliation
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (4 weeks): internal build + design of escrow UI and mapping heuristic. Phase 2 (6 weeks): pilot with 3 existing enterprise customers (opt-in), monitor operational load and cost delta. Phase 3 (8 weeks): refine heuristics, add legal T&Cs template, expand to invite list of early adopters. Full GA aligned with hosted-api-2025.03 if KPIs met.
risks: Customers find escrow model frictionful — mitigated by limiting hold window and offering concierge onboarding
Incorrect Commit Band mapping leads to underprovisioning — mitigate with conservative defaults and explicit canary windows
Billing disputes around refunds and prorations — require finance/T&Cs and clear messaging
Operational complexity in routing reserved requests to Dedicated vs hosted pools — requires ENG automation work and a fallback policy
notes: This mechanism is intentionally additive to existing intake scoring; it provides a contractual and technical lever to balance availability and cost. Consider integration points with Console (per-route dashboards), Redwood Dedicated reservations, and Private deployments for customers requiring isolation.
